title: SLO-anchored interrupt policy with progressive KV reservation
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Problem: Streaming/continuous batching prioritization currently relies on hard-cutoff preemption that causes tail-latency spikes for SLO-critical tenants and heavy KV cache churn. This ticket designs and implements an interrupt/preemption policy that is anchored to tenant SLOs and uses progressive KV reservations to reduce eviction churn and prevent GPU memory fragmentation. Goals: (1) enforce tenant latency SLOs with graceful, predictable interrupts; (2) reduce KV cache thrash under preemption by reserving incremental KV 'tokens' for in-flight slices; (3) avoid GPU memory fragmentation by coordinating preemption windows with defragment-friendly pause points; (4) expose observability for decision drivers so ops can adjust fairness parameters. Scope: runtime scheduler changes (preemptor), KV residency bookkeeping, metrics/tracing, simulation harness and k8s rollout for canary integration tests.
acceptance_criteria: SLO breach rate for P0 tenants decreases by >= 30% under mixed workloads compared to current baseline (measured in simulated 90th/99th percentile runs)
KV eviction rate (bytes/sec) reduces by >= 25% under heavy churn compared to current preemptor
No sustained increase in GPU memory fragmentation score (internal metric) after 1 hour of sustained load
New scheduler exposes decision trace: decision_reason, predicted_latency_headroom, kv_token_delta for each interrupt; traces appear in console and linkable to a request-id
Feature gated rollout flag with off-by-default configuration; unit and integration tests covering edge cases (long KV residency, small-batch microbursts, tenant-weighted fairness)
implementation_steps: Design: finalize algorithm for SLO-anchored interrupt budget and progressive KV tokens (this doc)
Runtime: implement interrupt policy in batch broker - tokenized reservation bookkeeping + soft-preempt handshake
KV layer: add reservation counters and a compacted eviction path that prioritizes non-reserved segments
GPU memory: add defragmentation-friendly pause points in model executor and track fragmentation metric
Sim: extend load generator to reproduce mixed-tenancy microburst patterns and validate metrics
CI: unit tests + end-to-end harness run in canary cluster with telemetry wired to console dashboards
Rollout: staged canary -> 10% -> 50% -> full with automated rollback on SLO/regression alerts
experiments: Compare conservative vs aggressive token growth curves (linear, logarithmic, cap) and pick the curve that minimizes tail latency while controlling KV usage
Measure impact of soft-preempt handshake (allowing micro-slices to finish) versus immediate interrupt on end-to-end latency and throughput
A/B test fragmentation-aware pause points frequency to find best trade-off between defragmentation overhead and interruption responsiveness
Stress test with 200 simultaneous tenants including synthetic P0 tenants to validate fairness weights and token exhaustion behavior
decisions: Use progressive token reservations (small initial token + capped growth) rather than fixed-size reservations to adapt to variable request lengths
Soft-preempt handshake chosen by default to reduce application-visible tail latency; hard-preempt path retained as emergency escape
Eviction will prefer non-reserved KV segments first; reserved segments are evicted only when preemption budget is exhausted
Expose two primary knobs: per-tenant SLO headroom (ms) and token-growth-curve (enum: linear/log/exp) to control fairness policy
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created; initial design sketched after runtime sync. Identified requirement to persist reservation counters per-lease rather than per-batch to survive short disconnects.
2026-03-03: Prototype token ledger implemented in dev branch; basic soft-preempt handshake messages serialized over broker channel. CPU integration tests green.
2026-03-06: KV layer changes implemented to mark segments reserved; observed 12% reduction in eviction ops in synthetic microburst run (dev infra).
2026-03-09: Simulated mixed workload: conservative token-growth improved P99 by 18% but used 14% more KV residency. Need to tune cap; opened PR for review.
2026-03-10: Design review with PM (Isha Patel) and SRE (Luca Rossi). PM requested dashboard views for per-tenant decisions; SRE requested rollout guardrail metrics and alert thresholds.
reviews_feedback: Isha Patel (PM): add explicit UX on console showing 'why' a tenant was preempted; prefer conservative default to protect KV for high-value tenants
Luca Rossi (SRE): require automated rollback trigger on >5% regression in 99th latency over 15-minute window; also request a playbook entry for emergency hard-preempt activation
Design review notes: prefer token growth cap at 3x average slice size to bound worst-case KV reservation
Code review (PR#8472): runtime bookkeeping implementation needs stronger unit tests around lease handoff; suggested tests for race between redeeming tokens and eviction path
rollout_plan: Feature gate default: off. Enable via runtime feature flag per cluster.
Canary: 1 node pair with synthetic workload for 6 hours; validate SLOs and KV eviction metrics
Gradual: 10% of traffic for 24 hours -> 50% for 48 hours -> full only after two consecutive healthy windows
Rollback: automatic if 99th latency regresses >5% over baseline or KV eviction rate increases >30%
Operational: add dashboard card + runbook section; schedule a 1-hour post-rollout review with SRE and product
notes: Next steps: tune token-growth cap and implement the lightweight tracing fields (decision_reason, kv_token_delta) into the request-level span. Coordinate with console team to add linkable traces. Schedule SRE run on canary day.
